::: {.eyebrow}
Water year 2024 · October 1, 2023 to September 30, 2024
:::

These are two pieces of music built from river gauges, weather stations, satellite plant-productivity data and fish counts. Every three days of data becomes one bar of music. Rising flow thickens the piano. Ice forming on the river brings in a falling glockenspiel and a bowed cymbal. Sockeye passing a dam climb the marimba. Nothing is a simple value-to-pitch beep: slow signals set the harmony, and faster ones set rhythm, texture and short motifs.

[Listen with the synced visual →](listen.qmd){.cta}

## The two pieces

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .piece-card}
### Granby River
Grand Forks, BC · key of D · 6:57

A warm El Niño winter. The gauge flagged ice on only 28 days, in broken spells, and the spring freshet came early and small: 147 m³/s, against 465 in the 2010–24 record.

<audio controls preload="none" src="listen/granby_wy2024.mp3"></audio>
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .piece-card}
### Okanagan
Okanagan Lake and River · key of F · 7:50

A drought year on the lake, which rose only 0.7 m. It was also the biggest sockeye return in ten years of Wells Dam counts: 491,039 fish.

<audio controls preload="none" src="listen/okanagan_wy2024.mp3"></audio>
:::
:::

## How to read this site

- **[Listen](listen.qmd)** shows each piece as tree rings: one ring per record, filling clockwise from October as the music plays, with a live readout of the date, the harmony and which instruments are sounding.
- **[Methods & code](methods.qmd)** explains every mapping from data to sound, the music theory behind the harmony, the quality checks, and the full source code.
